data.narrative:
DEEPX, a Series C semiconductor company, is valued at $529M post-money following $103M in total raised capital. The valuation is assessed against a comp universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private frontier-chip firms including Etched ($5.0B), Tenstorrent ($2.7B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and Positron AI ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the current $529M valuation, implying $899M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $2.4B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $5.0B. The peer cohort reflects material valuation dispersion, with Etched at the upper end and Positron AI at the lower bound.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $764M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median implied value of $1.6B. The current $529M valuation sits below the low-end estimate, suggesting potential undervaluation relative to peer-stage benchmarks. Key uncertainties include DEEPX's relative technical maturity, revenue traction, and addressable market positioning versus the heterogeneous peer set—particularly the variance between Series B and Series D stage peers—which materially widens the distribution and limits precision within the derived range.
